subject: Privilege proofing runbook + delivery slots for FinTechCo SIG packet
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security@fintechco.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ access artifacts: SCIM/SAML/RBAC samples + timeline

Marcus / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our SIG/CAIQ review we need a short bundle of access control artifacts to validate your provisioning and entitlement controls. Can you provide the following items by end of this week (EOW Apr 9)? If not, please propose the next-available delivery slot.

Required items:
- SCIM delta export covering the last 30 days (CSV or NDJSON) showing add/mod/remove events, timestamps, and source actor.
- 3 SAML assertion samples (raw XML) that show the NameID and attribute sets for: a user with standard product access, a service account used for telemetry ingestion, and a privileged admin.
- RBAC mapping document that maps Redwood roles to canonical FinTechCo roles (we'll use it to verify least-privilege claims).
- Short writeup of your process for reconciling SCIM deltas to entitlement changes (1 page).

Notes: we prefer redacted exports (no PII) when possible; if you need an MSA/NDA or a secure transfer location, flag that now. Also include any sample logs or runbook steps useful for auditors.

Contact here is Alice Zhang (security@fintechco.com).

Appreciate it — we want to keep the SIG close so the SOC+procurement review can proceed.

--
Alice Zhang
Security Engineer, FinTechCo
alice.zhang@fintechco.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ access artifacts: SCIM/SAML/RBAC samples + timeline

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a scoped bundle; a couple quick clarifying items so we scope correctly:

1) Redaction: we can remove PII (email addresses) from SCIM deltas and substitute stable opaque ids; is that acceptable for your audit team?
2) Service account sample: do you need runtime assertions (sampled from live auth flows) or synthetic assertion files generated from our STS for reproducibility?

Internal: I’ve looped in Laura (security lead) and Priyom (prod infra) to produce the artifacts. Neha — can you own the RBAC mapping writeup and the SAML sample collection? Priyom — can you produce a SCIM delta export and confirm the storage/location for secure transfer?

Proposed delivery windows (choose one):
- Option A: Wed Apr 7 morning (PST) — minimal redaction bundle + runbook draft
- Option B: Thu Apr 8 afternoon — full sample set + RBAC runbook

If FinTechCo needs earlier, we can prioritize Option A and follow up with a delta package.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Security Programs | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ access artifacts: SCIM/SAML/RBAC samples + timeline

Quick technical note — I can generate a SCIM delta CSV that includes:
- event_id, user_id (opaque), event_type (create/update/delete), timestamp (ISO8601), source (SSO / SCIM connector id), actor_id (system or admin id), and role_snapshot (pre/post roles)

Constraints / approach:
- We'll strip user emails and replace them with stable hashes to avoid PII leakage; we will keep created_at/updated_at and role snapshots as-is.
- For large accounts the delta export can be large; I'll provide a sampled compressed CSV for the last 30 days focused on provisioning activity (we can provide a full export under secure transfer if needed).
- Delivery plan: generate sample + integrity checksum (SHA256) and put in a password-protected share. I will also provide a short extraction log (scim-delta-script.log) so auditors can see the export command and filters used.

I can have the sample and script log ready for Option A (Wed Apr 7 09:00 PST).

—Priyom
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ access artifacts: SCIM/SAML/RBAC samples + timeline

Alice — attaching the RBAC mapping runbook and three SAML assertion samples. See attachments (stubs in this thread): saml-assertions-sample.txt, rbac-mapping-runbook.md.

Runbook highlights (summary):
- Mapping methodology: we map internal service roles (platform_admin, infra_operator, support_agent, telemetry_writer, product_user) to your canonical roles (Admin, Ops, Support, Integrations, EndUser). The markdown includes a matrix and a short FAQ for auditors.
- Least-privilege checks: we include a sampling of role assignments, service-account scopes, and how we enforce min-privilege during role rollouts.
- SAML samples: three raw assertions (privileged admin, service_account, product_user). Sensitive claim values have been redacted with placeholders where appropriate.

Attachments included in delivery package:
- rbac-mapping-runbook.md (mapping matrix + process)
- saml-assertions-sample.txt (3 raw XML assertions, redacted where necessary)

Transfer method: Priyom will upload the SCIM sample to a password-protected share and I will upload the RBAC + SAML files to the shared Drive link Marcus included. If you need a tighter channel (SFTP or secure Vault), tell us and we'll send a DocuSign/transfer link.

Planned delivery: Option A (Wed Apr 7 09:00 PST) for the redacted bundle. Full package (including unredacted export for on-prem review if requested) can follow under a separate data transfer agreement.

Thanks — we’ll await confirmation on redaction and the desired transfer mechanism.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 17:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ access artifacts: SCIM/SAML/RBAC samples + timeline

Marcus / team — thanks, this plan works. A couple quick clarifications before you bundle: 

- Redaction: yes, replace emails with opaque ids is fine. Please leave timestamp and role_snapshot intact.
- For the SAML assertion of the service account: could you include one example that shows the service_account scoped role "billing_admin" (we use that for our end-to-end entitlement validation)? If you can't release a real assertion with that exact role, document the attribute mapping that would contain it and include a synthetic example labeled as such.
- Transfer: password-protected Drive link is OK for the redacted bundle. For any unredacted export we will coordinate an SFTP channel and an NDA.

If you can deliver Option A Wednesday morning, we'll confirm receipt and then loop in our internal auditor for a quick verification.

Thanks — Alice
